title: When the Bridge Falls
premise: In the river town of Vellamark, on the eve of a revolution nobody can name yet, Isandro Okafor works as a typeface cutter's daughter in her father's print shop, keeping five years of learned silences. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the guild ledger holding every name in it — debtors, dissidents, the dead — she discovers her father cut a hidden second ledger into movable type, and the army wants it destroyed before anyone reads it. To get the truth on record ahead of the victors' historians, Isandro must ally with a conscripted officer who owes her his life and a smuggler who loved her once, printing forbidden pages by night while the bridge that carries both armies is rigged to fall. She succeeds at terrible cost: the truth survives in print, but her father dies for the type, her lover chooses duty over her, and justice arrives outside any law — delivered by her own hand and sealed in ink.
about_author: Isandro Halloran is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across river towns now erased from most maps. Their novels examine how ordinary tradespeople become accidental archivists of suppressed histories.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the Okafor print shop, Isandro sorts type while soldiers drill across the river, learning which questions her father answers and which he doesn't. The emotional beat is watchful unease — a household fluent in silence.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Army officers seize the town granary, billet troops in homes, and demand the guild ledger 'for audit.' Her father hands over a copy; Isandro notices the real pages are missing. Beat: fear sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Father Cut
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Searching the shop at night, she finds type slugs bearing names that appear in no ledger — dissidents, executed strikers, the disappeared. Her father catches her and finally speaks five years of silence. Beat: shattering revelation.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Owes
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Corvane's POV. Corvane, ordered to inventory and burn 'seditious print,' recognizes Isandro from the winter he nearly drowned under the ice and she pulled him out. Duty and debt collide. Beat: reluctant conscience awakening.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She and her father begin setting the hidden names as printable pages, working between inspections. A neighbor informant watches the shop too closely. Beat: conspiratorial intimacy shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Barge
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She seeks Tam Vey, the smuggler she once loved, to move paper and people past the blockade. He agrees — but wants the whole story, not fragments. Beat: old love rekindled into uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Neutral
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to arrest a printer in the next town, Corvane sees what 'audit' means there: gallows and ash. He begins falsifying his own reports. Beat: quiet treason taking root.

chapters.title: First Proof
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The first printed sheet of names comes off the press at 3 a.m., beautiful and damning. Her father weeps over the proof like a christening. Beat: fragile triumph before the storm.

chapters.title: The Informant's Price
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The neighbor denounces the shop; soldiers search and find nothing because Tam moved the type by barge hours earlier — but they take her father in for questioning. Beat: guilt and helplessness.

chapters.title: Interrogation Room Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane conducts the father's interrogation and deliberately botches it, buying time but marking himself. He warns Isandro through a coded receipt. Beat: two debts entangling into conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Bridge Has Two Sides
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam learns the army plans to blow the bridge when the revolution reaches the far bank, stranding the town as collateral. He brings this to Isandro: print fast or no one will be alive to read it. Beat: stakes made mortal.

chapters.title: A Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She adds living witnesses to the hidden edition — each name a person who must survive to confirm it. Recruiting them means breaking every silence she ever kept. Beat: courage compounding risk.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. His commander orders him to find the underground press within a week or face court-martial. He burns a decoy shipment and reports success. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Night Run on the River
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. A patrol boat chases the barge carrying the finished signature sheets; Tam scuttles half his cargo to escape, losing his livelihood to keep the pages. Beat: sacrifice without recognition.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Soldiers raze the print shop; her father refuses to flee, standing among his type. He is shot defending the formes. Isandro escapes with the master plates through the cellar tunnel. Beat: devastating loss.

chapters.title: Ash and Impression
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Grieving in Tam's hideout, she nearly burns the plates to end the danger. Corvane arrives, deserter now, carrying the army's execution lists — more names for the edition. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Printing in the Salt Caves
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Using a salvaged hand press in the salt caves below town, the three print the full edition: the dead, the living, the orders signed above them. Beat: sacred, exhausting labor of witness.

chapters.title: The Bridge Falls
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The charges detonate as the revolution crosses; the town is cut off, the army turns on its own garrison, and Corvane is caught helping civilians evacuate. Beat: chaos, climax igniting.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The commander who ordered the executions and the burning is captured by townsfolk who want a lynching. Isandro instead forces him to dictate a confession for the press before the crowd decides anything. Beat: moral climax — record over revenge.

chapters.title: What Tam Carried
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam runs the printed editions downriver to three cities ahead of the victors' historians, knowing he may not come back and that Isandro's heart was never fully his to keep. Beat: love released against duty's gravity.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the ruined market square, survivors read the true ledger aloud, name by name, while official historians arrive to find their version already obsolete. Corvane stands trial by the new council; Isandro testifies. Beat: reckoning and bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: Setting New Type
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Months later, Isandro rebuilds the shop on the ashes, cutting fresh type — including letters for names not yet written. She has learned which silences keep people safe, and which never did. Beat: hard-won peace, memory as craft.
